lettuce.text: A cultivated plant whose leaves are eaten in salads.

lilac.text: A shrub with fragrant violet, pink, or white blossoms.

lychee.text: A small rounded fruit with sweet white flesh and a rough red skin.

magnolia.text: A tree or shrub with large showy flowers.

mandrake.text: A Mediterranean plant with a forked root, once thought to have magical powers.

mango.text: A fleshy oval yellowish-red tropical fruit.

marigold.text: A plant with yellow or orange flowers.

marjoram.text: An aromatic plant of the mint family, used in cooking.

mistletoe.text: A parasitic plant with white berries, used as a Christmas decoration.

mulberry.text: A dark red or white fruit resembling the loganberry.

mustard.text: A hot-tasting yellow or brown paste made from seeds.

nasturtium.text: A trailing plant with round leaves and bright orange flowers.

nectarine.text: A variety of peach with smooth skin.

nutmeg.text: The hard aromatic seed of a tropical tree, used as a spice.

okra.text: A plant with long ridged seed pods eaten as a vegetable.

orchard.text: A piece of enclosed land planted with fruit trees.

orchid.text: A plant with complex, showy flowers.

oregano.text: An aromatic plant with leaves used as a culinary herb.

paprika.text: A powdered spice made from dried red peppers.

papaya.text: A tropical fruit shaped like an elongated melon.

parsley.text: A biennial plant with crinkly leaves used as a culinary herb.

parsnip.text: A long tapering cream-colored root vegetable.

passionfruit.text: The edible purple fruit of a passionflower.

peppermint.text: A plant of the mint family grown for its oil; a candy flavored with it.

persimmon.text: An edible fruit resembling a large tomato.

petunia.text: A plant with brightly colored funnel-shaped flowers.

pineapple.text: A large juicy tropical fruit with a tough segmented skin.

pomegranate.text: An orange-sized fruit with a tough reddish outer skin and many seeds.

poppy.text: A plant with showy red flowers and a milky sap.

potato.text: A starchy plant tuber that is one of the most important food crops.

primrose.text: A plant with pale yellow flowers.

quince.text: A hard, acid pear-shaped fruit used in preserves.

radicchio.text: A variety of chicory with dark red leaves.

radish.text: A pungent red root eaten raw.

raspberry.text: An edible soft fruit; a rude sound made with the tongue and lips.

rhododendron.text: A shrub with large clusters of bell-shaped flowers.

rosemary.text: An evergreen aromatic shrub used as a culinary herb.

sage.text: An aromatic herb; a profoundly wise person.

scallion.text: A long-necked onion with a small bulb.

scarecrows.text: Figures set up to scare birds away from crops.

snapdragons.text: Plants with flowers that open like a mouth.

sorghum.text: A cereal grown for grain and syrup.

soybean.text: A legume grown for its seeds, which are used as food.

squash.text: A gourd eaten as a vegetable; a racket game; to crush.

succulent.text: A plant with thick fleshy leaves adapted to store water.

tangerine.text: A small citrus fruit with a loose skin.

tarragon.text: A perennial plant with narrow aromatic leaves used as a herb.

thistle.text: A widely distributed plant with prickly leaves.

thyme.text: A low-growing aromatic plant of the mint family.

tomato.text: A glossy red fruit eaten as a vegetable.

topiary.text: The art of clipping shrubs into ornamental shapes.

tulip.text: A bulbous spring-flowering plant with cup-shaped flowers.

turnip.text: A round root with white or cream flesh, eaten as a vegetable.

zinnia.text: A plant with bright showy flowers.

anemone.text: A plant with brightly colored flowers; a sea anemone.

beagle.text: A small hound with a smooth coat and drooping ears.

nautilus.text: A cephalopod mollusk with a coiled chambered shell.

astronomy.text: The science of celestial objects and space.

canyon.text: A deep gorge, typically with a river flowing through it.

cavern.text: A large cave or chamber in a cave.

constellation.text: A group of stars forming a recognizable pattern.

cosmos.text: The universe seen as a well-ordered whole.

crevasse.text: A deep open crack in a glacier.

delta.text: A triangular tract of sediment at the mouth of a river.

dune.text: A mound or ridge of sand formed by the wind.

eclipse.text: An obscuring of the light from one celestial body by another.

equinox.text: The time when the sun crosses the celestial equator, making day and night equal.

horizon.text: The line at which the earth's surface and the sky appear to meet.

lightning.text: A high-voltage natural electrical discharge in the atmosphere.

mesa.text: An isolated flat-topped hill with steep sides.

meteor.text: A small body of matter from space that glows as it enters the atmosphere.

milestone.text: A stone marking distance; a significant stage or event.

mirage.text: An optical illusion caused by atmospheric conditions.

moor.text: A tract of open uncultivated upland.

nebulae.text: Clouds of gas and dust in outer space.

planet.text: A celestial body moving in an elliptical orbit around a star.

precipice.text: A very steep rock face or cliff.

ravine.text: A deep, narrow gorge with steep sides.

reef.text: A ridge of jagged rock or coral just above or below the sea's surface.

rocket.text: A cylindrical projectile propelled to a great height; a salad green.

satellite.text: A celestial body or artificial object orbiting a planet.

savanna.text: A grassy plain in tropical and subtropical regions.

seismograph.text: An instrument measuring and recording earthquakes.

sinkhole.text: A cavity in the ground caused by erosion or collapse.

smokestack.text: A chimney or funnel for discharging smoke.

solstice.text: Either of the two times each year when the sun reaches its highest or lowest point.

stalactite.text: A tapering structure hanging from the roof of a cave.

stalagmite.text: A mound or tapering column rising from the floor of a cave.

steppe.text: A large area of flat unforested grassland.

stratosphere.text: The layer of the atmosphere above the troposphere.

sunspot.text: A temporary dark spot on the sun's surface.

tectonic.text: Relating to the structure of the earth's crust.

thaw.text: To melt or become liquid after being frozen.

thunderhead.text: A rounded mass of cumulus cloud that often precedes a thunderstorm.

tidepool.text: A pool of water left on a beach by the ebbing tide (usually "tide pool").

tundra.text: A vast flat treeless Arctic region.

twilight.text: The soft glowing light from the sky when the sun is below the horizon.

volcano.text: A mountain with a crater through which lava erupts.

waterfall.text: A cascade of water falling from a height.

waterspout.text: A rotating column of water and spray formed by a whirlwind over the sea.

whirlpool.text: A quickly rotating mass of water.

whirlwind.text: A column of air moving rapidly around in a funnel shape.

wormhole.text: A hypothetical connection between widely separated regions of space-time.
